key_insight: Large language models can help abstract cancer registry variables from clinical reports, with best performance on simpler fields and weaker performance on exact date extraction.
clinical_relevance: If integrated carefully, LLMs could speed up cancer registry workflows and reduce manual abstraction burden, but their outputs still need human oversight for complex variables.
method: Evaluated 5 foundation LLMs with zero-shot prompting
Abstracted 8 registry variables from clinical reports
Tested on 5,939 patients across 7 cancer types
evidence_signal: Across a large real-world registry dataset, top models achieved about 0.8 F1 for low-cardinality variables and about 0.55 exact accuracy for diagnosis and treatment dates, improving to about 0.85 within a 30-day tolerance.
watch_item: Performance was lower for precise date extraction and smaller models underperformed, so deployment would require validation, error review, and workflow safeguards.
paper_title: Large language models for cancer registry abstraction: a real-world evaluation across models, variables, and cancer types
